test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who was the ruler of the Vijayanagara dynasty who ruled in the 16th century?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishnadeva Raya**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Krishnadeva Raya was the most powerful ruler of the **Vijayanagara Empire.**
 
• Raya expanded Vijayanagara through victories like the** Battle of Raichur (1520)**.
 
• He supported literature in Telugu, Kannada, Sanskrit, and Tamil, and wrote **Amuktamalyada.**
 
• He improved irrigation, agriculture, and tax systems for economic prosperity, he built temples and promoted religious harmony
 
• His death led to the gradual decline of Vijayanagara, which **fell after the 1565 Battle of Talikota. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulakeshin II**

 
 
• Pulakeshin II expanded the **Chalukya Empire (609–642 CE**), defeating Harshavardhana and other regional powers.
 
• He made Vatapi (Badami) the capital and promoted architecture, including **rock-cut temples.**
 
• Pulakeshin II was defeated and killed by Pallava king Narasimhavarman I in 642 CE, leading to the fall of Vatapi.
 
 
 
• **Raja Raja Chola**
 
 
• Raja Raja Chola expanded the empire through conquests in **South India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives,** making the Cholas a dominant naval power.
 
• He commissioned the construction of the Brihadeshwara Temple in **Thanjavur, **a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture.
 
• Raja Raja Chola reformed administration by organizing the empire into provinces (mandalams) and revamping revenue collection systems.
 
 
 
• **Adi Shankara**
 
 
• Adi Shankara is renowned for consolidating the Advaita Vedanta philosophy, which emphasizes the non-duality of the soul (Atman) and Brahman (the ultimate reality).
 
• He founded** four major mathas** (monastic centers) in **Sringeri**,** Dwaraka, Puri, and Jyotirmath **to spread and preserve Vedic knowledge.
 
• Adi Shankara wrote influential commentaries on key Hindu scriptures, including the Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and Brahmasutras, promoting the **Vedantic school of thought.**
